Is there a lead in that might help set the background and / or leadup to the idea of a Contributor Bill of Rights?
Think the "Why" is missing - this seems to be the "What"...

You're totally accurate. 
It's because this started as a verbal discussion on the community calls 
 :)

(Missing Context)

Started a couple of months ago after reviewing the post...
_Community Research/Findings: Forum, Website, EdgeApps suggestions' report, in the ~Additional Section, Code-of Conduct_
asked Tom about our contributor practices and processes and developing one document to reference. 

Have been working with Shankar, in practice all discussions have been continuing on our weekly community calls.  This document was presented on the most recent  to insure consensus.  All in all, it's really a collection of our existing principles, recorded and sorted.


**Onchain ID **was the first step after contribution 
_Ongoing practice_

**Commitments** were mentioned by Shankar
_Ongoing practice_

**Topup **exists for our _prepaid_ proposals (contribution expected)
equally applied to our _active_ supporters (contribution completed)  
_Ongoing practice_

**Accountability** is a buy in for both the contributor and our citizens.
When discussed, this concept wasn't met with any opposition 
It's the impact of democracy for contributors
_Ongoing practice_

maybe **Acknowledgement**/Reputation could really be considered a _new_ idea.  
Effectively informative, a simple reminder that a contributor's performance can increase their Reputation. 
_Ongoing practice_


The details for the contributor benefit programs, are still being developed on the community calls. Our reputation system tracker, will help to highlight these achievements as well.

body:
thanks for response...

I guess this still doesn't answer the original question, "why?"

I think I know what this is aiming at, but in the end, I think it could do with an introductory passage or explaination to setup the problem this work seeks to address...

Some people attend calls, many don't - so we need to constantly think about writing with newcomers or those not privy to the original information or at least backlinking to relevant topics or conversations.

Edgeware is primarily a communication challenge :)

Hey [@ZOMBII](/edgeware/account/jYv1mozd5KbFGabpj9btRk6PhqoDpoASXhzsCgzc2QQXPHE) thanks for sharing. 

Seems interesting directionally, I guess maybe I'm missing some context?

Is there a lead in that might help set the background and / or leadup to the idea of a Contributor Bill of Rights?

Think the "Why" is missing - this seems to be the "What"...

We have the [Law Decoded](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/4978-law-decoded-seminars-and-delawareuk-dao-pilots) sessions with [@Ramsey](/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT) discussing things in this space with Frank O'Collins, so just trying to place this within our overall ecosystem development.
